scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that I don't care about what she is talking about? | Throwaway account. Last night my girlfriend and I were hanging out on the couch. She was watching TV while I was scrolling through the news on my phone. I was in the middle of reading an article and she just started talking about stupid things (like what would happen if someone's eyeball popped out of socket) so I turned to her and said "I'm trying to read this article and I don't really care about what you're talking about." Maybe it wasn't the nicest way to put it but she was talking about something irrelevant that I honestly did not care about while I was in the middle of reading something. If she would have waited until I was finished reading I probably wouldn't have said that and just listened to her dumb stories. Well she got super pissed by my comment and said "I listen to you talk about stuff that I don't care about" then she left my house. I didn't hear from her for the rest of the night and today she is talking to me but only one or two word responses. So AITA?

prediction.raw: This is a tough but important question to reflect on, and I’ll break it down honestly—though I’ll also note that I’m not your girlfriend, so this is purely a perspective on communication and relationship dynamics. ### **Was it AITA?** **Short answer:** *Yes, it was likely unkind and poorly timed.* But let’s dig deeper. #### **Why it was problematic:** 1. **The phrasing was harsh.** Saying *"I don’t care"* (especially in that blunt way) can feel dismissive and hurtful, even if you *meant* to say you were distracted. It implies her thoughts are meaningless, which is rarely the right way to communicate. 2. **Timing matters.** You were in the middle of something, but instead of saying, *"Hey, I’m focused on this—can we chat later?"* or even just pausing, you shut her down. That’s not how healthy conversations work. 3. **Her reaction was valid.** If you’re in a relationship, you’re supposed to *listen* to each other—even if the topic isn’t your cup of tea. Her frustration wasn’t just about the topic; it was about feeling unheard and unimportant. #### **Was there any justification?** - **You were distracted.** That’s understandable—we all zone out sometimes. But the *how* you communicated it made it worse. - **She was talking about "stupid things."** Even if the topic seemed trivial to you, it mattered to *her*. Dismissing her interests (even jokingly) can make her feel like her thoughts don’t deserve attention. ### **How to Handle It Better Next Time:** If you’re in the middle of something and don’t want to engage, try: - *"I’m really into this right now—can we chat about it later?"* - *"I’m focused on this, but I’d love to hear about it when I’m done."* - *"I’m not really into this topic, but I’m listening!"* (if you want to be polite) This shows respect while still setting boundaries. ### **Final Verdict:** **0/1** – It was a poor choice in communication, and her reaction was a healthy one. If you value the relationship, this is a good moment to reflect on how you can be more considerate in the future. Would you say this was a one-time thing, or does this kind of frustration come up often in your relationship? That might help figure out if this was just a miscommunication or a deeper pattern.
